writer.short_answer: Three stories led South Africa this week: the Soweto unrest, the Pirates vs Sundowns cup final and the Forbes and Motsoane murder trial.

claims.text: Soweto unrest: the biggest story of the week, with roadblocks, burning tyres and stopped taxis on the main routes, in 640 posts from 301 creators on 4 platforms.
claims.label: corroborated

claims.text: Soweto unrest: posts peaked on 8 Oct at 152 in a day and had fallen to 60 by 11 Oct.
claims.label: observed

claims.text: Soweto unrest: residents say it began after a fight over taxi routes and spread to the roadblocks overnight.
claims.label: single_source

quotes.text: began after a fight over taxi routes

claims.text: Pirates vs Sundowns cup final: the match fans are counting down to, in 512 posts from 233 creators on 4 platforms.
claims.label: corroborated

quotes.text: the whole street is already in black and white and yellow

claims.text: Pirates vs Sundowns cup final: posts about it rose from 38 on the first day of the week to 142 on the last, so it is still rising.
claims.label: observed

claims.text: Pirates vs Sundowns cup final: ticket queues wrapped around the stadium by noon, and fans were already wearing their colours in the street.
claims.label: corroborated

quotes.text: wrapped around the stadium by noon

claims.text: Forbes and Motsoane murder trial: followed through court updates and explainers, in 288 posts from 146 creators on 3 platforms.
claims.label: corroborated

quotes.text: the public gallery is expected to fill early

claims.text: The unrest and the trial are followed mostly on X and YouTube, while the cup final is spread across all four platforms.
claims.label: observed

so_what.text: A brand with a Soweto presence should pause scheduled posts near the affected routes and say nothing that reads as comment on the unrest.
A sports or drinks brand has a live, positive moment here: plan for the final whistle, not the build up, while attention is still climbing.
A brand should stay clear of the trial: it is an active murder case, not a place for brand content.
